title: Priority lanes and evaluation flow for customer-driven model variant additions, pin requests, and deprecations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Enterprise customers are increasingly requesting on-ramps for specific model variants, version pins, and controlled deprecations. Current intake is ad-hoc: CS sends requests to PM, engineering triages case-by-case, and design/UX often only looped in late. This causes long lead times, inconsistent QA/eval coverage, and operational surprises during rollouts.

Problem statement: We need a lightweight, repeatable prioritization and eval flow for customer-driven catalog changes (new model variants, pins, and deprecation requests) that balances enterprise SLAs, quality guarantees, and platform capacity. The flow should enable predictable SLAs for enterprise customers, clear engineering scope, and measurable rollback criteria.

Goal: Create priority lanes (FastTrack, Standard, Deferred) and an associated evaluation checklist and gating rules that allow PM/Eng to triage incoming requests within 3 business days and surface a recommended lane. The outcome should reduce decision latency, align expectations with customers, and reduce emergency rollouts by 50% in 3 months.
acceptance_criteria: Documented intake form template for customer requests with required fields (use-case summary, expected traffic, data sensitivity, SLA requirement, reason for pin/deprecation)
Triage rubric published in Confluence with scoring rules and automatic lane recommendation (FastTrack, Standard, Deferred)
Eval-gate checklist created (functional correctness, safety/regression smoke tests, perf profile, quantization compatibility, fallback plan)
Playbook for pinning and deprecation that includes rollback criteria, communication templates, and monitoring dashboards
SLO: 90% of incoming requests are assigned a lane within 3 business days
At least one pilot with an enterprise customer completed end-to-end using the new flow and retrospective documented
proposal: 1) Intake: Create a standardized intake form (Google Form + webhook into Linear) capturing technical, business, and compliance signals. 2) Triage rubric: Numeric scoring (0-10) across axes: customer strategic value, security/compliance risk, technical risk (inference compatibility), performance impact, and maintenance burden. 3) Priority lanes: - FastTrack: high-strategic value + low technical risk => target 2 week turn. - Standard: moderate value or medium risk => 4-8 week plan. - Deferred: low immediate value or high risk => schedule to backlog with periodic review. 4) Eval gates: Minimum test set (customer prompt set + Redwood smoke prompts), safety regression checks, perf/latency benchmark vs. baseline, quantization test (if applicable), and rollback instrumentation. 5) Operationalization: Templates for pin request PRs, deployment checklist, monitoring dashboard widgets, and CS/AM communication templates.
scope: In-scope: intake form, triage rubric, lane definitions, eval-gate checklists, pilot with 1-2 enterprise accounts, Confluence docs, dashboard prototypes, and launch playbook. Out-of-scope: changes to runtime autoscaling, billing model, or major console UI redesign (console UI tweaks for rollout pages allowed).
success_metrics: Decision latency: median time from request to lane assignment <= 3 business days
Rollout incidents: reduce emergency rollback events related to customer pins by 50% over 90 days
Predictability: >= 80% of FastTrack requests meet the advertised turnaround (2 weeks)
Customer satisfaction: CS NPS / satisfaction score for the pin onboarding flow >= 8/10 in pilot feedback
risks: Underestimating integration work for certain model families (e.g., models requiring custom kernels or unusual tokenizers)
Hidden data governance requirements for enterprise customers that extend timeline (legal/compliance hold)
Resource contention with core runtime or infra teams causing lane SLAs to slip
Over-indexing on FastTrack leads to technical debt (too many pinned variants to support long-term)
dependencies: Legal: one-off contract addenda for enterprise data processing (if required)
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Build intake form and triage rubric; sketch eval-gate checklist. Week 3-5: Implement webhook -> Linear automation and Confluence pages; align ENG on test harness requirements. Week 6-8: Pilot with 1 enterprise customer (AM-led); run full eval gates and do one controlled pin. Week 9: Collect feedback, iterate, and publish playbook + templates. Post-launch: monthly review of deferred queue and quarterly capacity gating. Escalation path: emergency rollbacks follow runtime incident runbook and PM-led customer comms templates.
notes: Decision: prefer numeric rubric over categorical heuristics to improve reproducibility and enable future automation
Trade-off: FastTrack will carry stricter post-rollout monitoring requirements to limit long-term maintenance cost
Suggestion from Solutions: add a revenue or contract-risk multiplier to the rubric to prioritize strategic customers
